label: NOTE: THE GUARDED STORE IS WRITTEN OUT FIVE TIMES, so every anchor into one of them carries its arm's comment or its following statement with it.  The object repeats the block at all five sites (D500) and factoring it into a helper would move the source away from the object, so finding 1264's trap applies here at five times over: a bare `if (word_cac <= V90CP_BITS - 1) {` matches five times, mutate.py calls that UNUSABLE, and UNUSABLE DOES NOT FAIL A RUN.
why: Recorded here because the same shape defeated three anchors in v90mp.json and two in this tree's own suites.

label: the run counters are swapped
why: +0xca9 counts ones and +0xcaa zeros; swapping them stops the preamble ever completing.

label: Ed is read from a local rather than back out of the object
why: The object stores 0 into +0xcaa on a one bit and reloads it four instructions later, so a group size of zero makes the test true on a ONE.  Guarding on `bit == 0` is what a cached counter would behave like, and the zero-group corner is what kills it.

label: Ed does not require the cursor to be home
Ed answers V90MP's 3 rather than 5
sixteen ones are enough for the preamble
why: `cmp $0x10,%cl` / `jbe`, so it takes SEVENTEEN.  The test feeds sixteen and a zero and reads the blob's state back.

label: the preamble hands over to state 2 rather than 1
the framing zero test is inverted
the type bit selects the wrong form
the type bit is not stored
the short form is sixteen bits, not fifteen
the three block flags land in the wrong fields
the flag block is four bits, not three
the header ends at 0x32 rather than 0x33
why: `evaluateInfo`'s case 5 stores 0x32 into the READ cursor and the write cursor stops one past it.  The two halves were read independently and agree.

label: the next block is chosen in the wrong order
why: +0x04, then +0x08, then +0x0c, which is the order the blocks travel.

label: the pairs block ends at 0x98 rather than 0x99
the pairs block hands over to 10 whatever +0x08 says
the four counts are four frames of sixteen, not seventeen
alpha is sixteen bits to the entry, not seventeen
why: One frame per entry: a framing bit and sixteen information bits.

label: alpha counts only the first three lists
the lists block is bounded by beta rather than alpha
why: alpha is +0x8 in .bss and beta +0xc, and the object compares this arm against the first.

label: the values and counts block is four frames, not five
beta is sixteen bits to the entry, not seventeen
find:
beta = 17 * (nof_buf[0] + nof_buf[1] + nof_buf[2] +
				     nof_buf[3] + nof_buf[4] + nof_buf[5]);
replace:
beta = 16 * (nof_buf[0] + nof_buf[1] + nof_buf[2] +
				     nof_buf[3] + nof_buf[4] + nof_buf[5]);

find:

label: the buffers block is bounded by alpha rather than beta
the CRC frame is sixteen bits, not seventeen
why: One framing zero and sixteen CRC bits.

label: the CRC extent is one past the cursor
why: `infoToBits` computes the same number as start + 0x11 from the other side.

label: the CRC verdict is inverted
a bad CRC does not reset the detector
the bad-CRC line is spelled correctly
why: "recieved" is the author's.  The transcript is compared as text between the two sides.

label: the tail waits on the group size rather than on six
why: Finding 4364: the transmitter pads to a whole number of +0x3ba8 and the receiver hardcodes six.  The suite sweeps the group size over 1..6, 12 and 17.

label: the tail's bit test is inverted
the tail does not reset the detector before reporting
the answer reads the two bits the wrong way round
bitsToInfo returns nothing
why: A return type is not mangled, so `void` had to be read out of the epilogues.  Both `ret`s move %edi into %eax.

label: the hold-off suppresses 1 and 3 rather than 2 and 4
the hold-off is started by 3 and 4 rather than by 1 and 2
the hold-off runs to 0x321
the hold-off never stops
the bound is one too high in the short form's arm
why: `cmp $0x2edf` / `ja`: 0x2edf is the last index that fits, and 0x2ee0 is crc[0].

label: the lists arm is not bounded at all
the header arm IS bounded, where the object leaves it open
why: D500: five of the ten store sites carry the check and five do not, and case 5 is one of the five that do not.  Adding it changes what happens at 0x2ee0.

label: the overrun line loses the author's spelling
why: "enouch", the space before the comma, the space before the trailing newline and the LEADING newline are all in .rodata.str1.4+0xd650.
find: "\n *** error CP bit , not enouch memory in the buffer *** \n"
